nodes.title: The adversary for online bipartite matching

nodes.summary: Every matching has at most twice as many edges as the greedy one. An edge of the matching whose right vertex the greedy algorithm matched is charged to that right vertex, any other edge to its left vertex, which the greedy algorithm matched by maximality; a matching charges each greedy edge at most once on each side.
nodes.title: Greedy online matching is `1/2`-competitive

nodes.summary: In a bipartite graph, the maximum matching computed by augmenting paths has at most twice as many edges as the greedy online matching, in which the right vertices arrive in increasing order.
nodes.title: Greedy online matching is within a factor $2$ of the maximum

nodes.summary: Given a partner array, which assigns to each right vertex its partner on the left if it has one, the right vertices of a list $S$ are done when, for every right vertex $j$ of $S$ and every left vertex $i$ adjacent to $j$, $j$ is matched or $i$ is matched.

nodes.title: The $1/2$ lower bound with a matching of the arrivals' graph

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a sequence of arrivals (neighbour lists) and $m$ a perfect matching of $\sigma$. Then the bipartite graph of $\sigma$, in which left vertex $i$ is adjacent to arrival $j$ when $i$ lies in the $j$-th neighbour list, has a matching with as many edges as $\sigma$ has arrivals.

nodes.summary: In a bipartite graph with left vertices $0, \dots, a - 1$ and right vertices $0, \dots, b - 1$, the greedy online matching is the partner array obtained by starting from the empty matching and letting the right vertices arrive in the order $0, 1, \dots, b - 1$, each arriving vertex being matched to its first free left neighbour in the order $0, \dots, a - 1$, or left unmatched if no neighbour is free.

nodes.title: Greedy run on an array

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a list of distinct right vertices, all unmatched in a valid partner array $m$, and let $S$ be a list of right vertices that are done for $m$. Then the partner array obtained from $m$ by the greedy run along $L$ is valid, and every right vertex of $L$ or of $S$ is done for it.

nodes.summary: The set of pairs $(i, j)$ such that the greedy online matching assigns the left vertex $i$ to the right vertex $j$ is a matching of the bipartite graph.
nodes.title: The greedy online matching is a matching

nodes.summary: For every online matcher $A$, every list $h$ of earlier neighbour lists and every list of gadgets with distinct vertices, the adversary's offline matching for $A$, $h$ and the gadgets is a perfect matching of the adversary's arrivals for $A$, $h$ and the gadgets. In each gadget, the first arrival takes the vertex the second one does not.
nodes.title: The adversary's arrivals have a perfect matching

nodes.summary: A list $m$ of left vertices is a perfect matching of a sequence $\sigma$ of arrivals (neighbour lists) when $m$ and $\sigma$ have the same length, the entries of $m$ are pairwise distinct, and for each $j$ the $j$-th entry of $m$ lies in the $j$-th neighbour list of $\sigma$.

nodes.title: Graph of a sequence of arrivals

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
